newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Lesotho mutiny sparks anxiety over water project.
newsitem.headline: Lesotho mutiny sparks anxiety over water project.

text.p: South Africa was worried that the police mutiny in neighbouring Lesotho could distrupt the next stage of the multi-million rand Lesotho Highlands water project, Water Affairs and Forestry Minister Kader Asmal said on Tuesday.

"Political instability does not help in forward planning and particularly when the next phase of the project may involve the removal of 2,500 families, and resettlement is always a very sensitive issue," Asmal said told a parliamentary media briefing.

He said the government was "anxious" about the situation because of outstanding issues in the treaty on the water project which will see surplus water diverted from Lesotho to South Africa's main industrial centres.

Eight officers of Royal Lesotho Mounted Police, resisting arrest for the killings of three fellow officers in 1995, seized control of the country's police headquarters last Thursday and dismissed the police commissioner who was abroad at the time.
A meeting of Lesotho's senior police on Monday however resolved to set up a committee to negotiate an end to the dispute.

Asmal said South Africa's neighbour had been politically stable for some time, but added: "It makes it more difficult when you have to make choices when there is an element of uncertainty in a country where the project is the centre of the economic and social life."
